title: Microsoft Dataverse: management MCP server for building and governing MCP servers
summary: Pass: the roadmap facts, documented control paths and commands are supported, and the briefing appropriately distinguishes the management endpoint from surrounding controls. The general premium-connector licensing statement needs an additional citation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The management reference does not publish a charge.
claims.quote: Searched: "mcp-management" licensing billing; management MCP server MCPManagement licensing price DLP access control roles disable audit. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-management in full and /microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing; no management-server charge stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn marks the management server reference as preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Consuming Copilot Studio agents may use Copilot Credits under their existing billing model.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the common currency across Copilot Studio capabilities. You can get them through pay-as-you-go meters, prepurchase plans, and Copilot Credit prepaid pack subscriptions.

claims.claim: Whether premium connectors need a licence depends on the consuming product and its licence.
claims.quote: If an instant flow has premium connectors, every user who runs the flow needs a Power Automate Premium license. In such cases, instead of licensing every user, you can license the flow with a Process license.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/faqs#how-do-power-automate-license-plans-work-for-flow-runs to sources for this general statement; the existing Copilot Studio billing source already documents premium connectors under its standalone subscription.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits constrain underlying Dataverse API calls.
claims.quote: To ensure consistent availability and performance for everyone, Dataverse applies limits to how APIs are used. These limits detect when client applications make extraordinary demands on server resources.

claims.claim: The cited Dataverse limits are not a published quota or pricing meter specific to the management server.
claims.quote: Searched: "mcp-management" licensing billing; management MCP server MCPManagement licensing price DLP access control roles disable audit. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/api-limits and /microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-management; no management-specific quota or meter found.

claims.claim: Dataverse data-endpoint availability is managed in Power Platform admin center under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server.
claims.quote: Select **Manage** > **Environments**. ... select **Settings**. Under **Settings**, select **Product** > **Features**. Scroll down to locate **Dataverse Model Context Protocol** and make sure **Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server** is turned on.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the Dataverse data-endpoint availability switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse MCP server disable environment setting PowerShell Power Platform API organization Web API allow MCP clients; "Dataverse" "MCP" "pac admin" "disable". Read configuration page, Dataverse CLI reference and pac admin search excerpts; no switch operation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented that the Dataverse environment switch governs the management endpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: "management MCP server" disable governance access controls audit licensing; "management MCP server" "access". Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-mcp-disable and /microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-management; no relationship stated.

claims.claim: Dataverse client allow listing is managed under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled.
claims.quote: Select **Advanced Settings**. ... The list of available clients is shown. Open the client record you want. ... On the MCP client record, set **Is Enabled** to **Yes**.

claims.claim: dataverse mcp allow <appId> adds an application to the target Dataverse environment's allowed MCP clients.
claims.quote: Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment. ... dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options]

claims.claim: The Dataverse CLI is preview.
claims.quote:
# Dataverse CLI reference (preview)

Note

- This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The CLI allow operation requires Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.
claims.quote: The authenticated user must have Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint.
claims.quote: MCP allow listing applies only to the `/api/mcp` agent entrypoint. MCP-named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and aren't restricted by this setting.

claims.claim: A registered MCP server can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for this Agent 365 server-blocking control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph API block MCP server Agent 365 tools registry tool management; "MCP" "block" "graph/api" Agent 365. Read manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp reference excerpt: CLI block removed; no equivalent Graph operation found.

claims.claim: The server-blocking action is tenant-wide and disables all tools exposed by the selected server.
claims.quote: Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization ... Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.

claims.claim: Individual tools are managed by selecting the MCP server, opening Tools and changing the tool toggle.
claims.quote: Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle. ... Turn individual tools on or off as needed.

claims.claim: Individual tool control is limited to supported server types and experiences using the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365. ... The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the policy at runtime for supported tools and experiences that use the gateway.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 controls are not documented as governing direct management-endpoint calls.
claims.quote: Searched: "management MCP server" "access"; Microsoft Graph API block MCP server Agent 365 tools registry tool management. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and /microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-management; direct-call coverage not established.

claims.claim: A connector data policy can be created in Power Platform admin center under Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote: select **Security** ... select **Data and privacy**. ... select **Data policy**. ... select **New Policy** to create a new policy to configure.

claims.where: Governance controls prose: Advanced connector policies

claims.quote: administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server. As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available.
